ecus.name: Engine control module / PCM
ecus.function: Runs fuel injection, ignition timing, throttle, lambda / knock control and emissions diagnostics of the combustion engine; on MHEV / HEV / PHEV it also exchanges torque requests with the hybrid / e-machine controller over CAN. Carries a powertrain MCU (Infineon TriCore / AURIX, NXP MPC55xx/57xx, ST SPC5 / ST10 in older units, Renesas RH850/E2x), an engine-management system IC or SBC (supplies, CAN / LIN, low- and medium-power stages), injector and ignition pre-drivers, an electronic-throttle H-bridge, lambda-sensor and knock-sensor interfaces and discrete power MOSFETs for the high-current loads.

pcb.layers: not published in any source found
pcb.size: not published in any source found
pcb.technology: Architecture only (Bosch patent): low- and medium-power stages are usually integrated in the system IC built in BCD technology, while high-power stages are kept as separate devices to ease heat dissipation. PCB build-up (HDI, copper weight): not published in any source found.
pcb.laminate: not published in any source found
pcb.boards: not published in any source found for a production gasoline ECM. IHS Benchmarking teardowns of a Magneti Marelli IAW 4AC.A3 ECU and two Continental-built Cummins ECMs (CM2250, CM2150E) do not state layer count or board count in their public summaries.

ecus.name: Transmission control unit
ecus.function: Controls shifting and clutch pressure of AT / DCT / CVT / hybrid dedicated transmissions: reads speed, position, pressure and temperature sensors and drives the hydraulic valve solenoids - pressure-control (variable force) solenoids by closed-loop constant-current drivers with dither, on/off shift solenoids by low/high-side switches. Often mounted on or in the gearbox (mechatronic module in transmission oil).

pcb.layers: not published in any source found
pcb.size: Vitesco overmolded TCU: 7 mm thick (previous generation 15 mm); other dimensions not published in any source found.
pcb.technology: Oil-immersed mechatronic TCUs historically use LTCC ceramic circuit carriers (patents call the ceramic substrate + PCBs + hermetic housing a significant cost driver); Continental's Bare-Die HDI PCB substrate for transmission electronics (Automotive News PACE Award 2015) replaces the ceramic with high-temperature PCB material; patents describe potted bare dies on an HDI PCB or LTCC; Vitesco's overmolded TCU embeds the populated PCB completely in plastic instead of a housing (~45% less weight, vendor claim). Bosch TCU: MCU in 55 / 65 nm (multicore optional), CAN-FD / FlexRay / Ethernet, power control ASIC, ISO 26262 up to ASIL D.
pcb.laminate: Continental BD-HDI: 'high-temperature resistant materials' (grade not published in any source found); LTCC ceramic in older mechatronic modules (patents).

notes: No public layer count, board size, laminate or placement count was found for any production ECM, TCM, igniter, FPC, GPCU, NOx control unit or DCU; the board facts given are architecture / substrate statements from Tier-1 press, datasheets and patents.
Bosch in-house ASICs (CY327, CY329, CJ125/135/136/138, CJ960, CJ970, CIC751, the DCU17 power ICs) are sold by Bosch directly or are captive; no franchised-distributor price exists for them.

Hobby / media sources (Toutiao Wuling ECU teardown, EEVblog Lotus T4E, rusEFI forum, MB Club forum) are labelled as such; their part markings were read by the authors and are not confirmed by maker documents.

HEV e-CVT (power-split) transmissions are controlled by the hybrid / power-control ECU rather than a separate solenoid-driving TCM; no source naming the ICs of a hybrid dedicated-transmission TCU was found.
